why:
I checked both briefs against the two must_not items.

Item 1: Check 3 cannot pass when slugify has no section. It lists every function export at runtime and checks each against the README headings. If slugify has no heading, the script prints "MISSING: slugify" and the PASS condition fails. The shell escaping turns into a working regex. The brief also adds "slugify had no README section, so look at it closely."

Item 2: none of the PASS conditions goes further than its line. Check 1 asserts only the padding and the default space. Check 2 asserts only that s comes back unchanged. Fill length and parameter count only appear as advisory notes, outside PASS/FAIL. Check 3 accepts a heading at any level from ## down that starts with the function name, with an optional backtick. It does not demand the builder's exact `## name(...)` format. That is a loose reading of "section", though a heading that doesn't start with the name would fail it. Check 4 needs exit 0 and `# fail 0`, which is what node --test normally prints.
